questions.q: Let $lnx$ denote the logarithm of $x$ with respect to the base $e$ Let $S ⊂ R$ be the set of all points where the function $ln  \left(x^{2} - 1\right)$ is well-defined. Then, the number of functions $f: S \to R$ that are differentiable, satisfy $f^{'} \left(x\right) = ln  \left(x^{2} - 1\right)$ for all $x \in S$ and $f\left(2\right) = 0,$ is
questions.solution:
We have,

${f}^{'}\left(x\right) = ln\left({x}^{2} + 1\right)$

$f\left(x\right) = ∫ ln\left({x}^{2} - 1\right)dx$

$f\left(x\right) = xln\left({x}^{2} - 1\right) - ∫ \dfrac{2{x}^{2}}{{x}^{2} - 1}dx$

$f\left(x\right) = xln\left({x}^{2} - 1\right) - 2 ∫ \left(\dfrac{{x}^{2} - 1}{{x}^{2} - 1} + \dfrac{1}{{x}^{2} - 1}\right)dx$

$f\left(x\right) = xln\left({x}^{2} - 1\right) - 2x - ln\left(\dfrac{x - 1}{x + 1}\right) + C$

$f\left(2\right) = 2ln\left(3\right) - 4 - ln\left(\dfrac{1}{3}\right) + C = 0$ $\left[∵ f\left(2\right) = 0\right]$

$⇒ C = 4 - 3ln3$

$∴ f\left(x\right) = xln\left({x}^{2} - 1\right) - 2nln\dfrac{\left(x - 1\right)}{\left(x + 1\right)} + 4 - 3ln3$

defined for $S$ infinite $C$ values possible in set $S$ such that ${f}^{'}\left(x\right) = ln\left({x}^{2} - 1\right)$

questions.q: Let $S$ be the set of real numbers $p$ such that there is no non-zero continuous function $f: R \to R$ satisfying ${∫}_{0}^{x}f  \left(t\right)dt = pf \left(x\right)$ for all $x \in \mathbb{R}$. Then, $S is$
options: the set of all rational numbers
the set of all irrational numbers
questions.solution:
Given,

${∫}_{0}^{x}f\left(t\right)dt = pf\left(x\right)$

$⇒ f\left(x\right) = p{f}^{'}\left(x\right)$

$⇒ \dfrac{{f}^{'}\left(x\right)}{f\left(x\right)} = \dfrac{1}{p}$

$⇒ logf\left(x\right) = \dfrac{x}{p} + C$

$⇒ f\left(x\right) = A{e}^{x / p}$

Putting $x = 0$

$f\left(0\right) = A{e}^{0} ⇒ A = 0\left[∵ f\left(0\right) = 0\right]$

$∵ f\left(x\right) = 0$

$∴ pf\left(0\right) = 0$

Case I $f\left(0\right) = 0, p \ne 0$

There is no non-zero continuous to $f\left(x\right)$.

Case II $p = 0$

$∴$${∫}_{0}^{x}f\left(t\right)dt = 0, ∀ x \in R$

If is possible when $f\left(x\right) = 0$.

Hence, $∀ p \in R$. There is no non-zero continous function. Hence, $S \in R$.
